one_liner: Administrative and operations backbone for an ICE ERO field office: budget, procurement, HR, space, property, travel, and running the vehicle fleet program.
fit_summary: This is open to the public under Direct Hire Authority, so your lack of federal status and veterans' preference does not hurt you, and your IEM government-client work may map to coordination, reporting, and liaison duties. The fit depends on whether your IEM role involved hands-on administrative work such as budget, logistics, vendors, travel, or data analysis at a GS-09 (for GS-11) or GS-11 (for GS-12) level. Your policy knowledge matters less here than operational and administrative detail.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring paths: public and federal transition); Direct Hire Authority applies, so category rating and veterans' preference do not apply.

GS-11 requires one year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-09 in 3 or more of these areas: coordinating administrative projects, solving administrative problems, analyzing administrative data, preparing reports, or representing the office with vendors and support organizations.

GS-12 requires one year at the GS-11-equivalent level in 3 or more of these areas: independent evaluations, advising on management programs, making agreements and commitments, or liaison work. Alternatively, a Ph.D., 3 years of graduate study, or an LL.M. can qualify you for GS-11 only, with transcripts required.
Requires a Secret security clearance; expect a background investigation before you start.
You must meet all qualifications by the closing date of October 30, 2026; confirm the specific duty locations listed under Multiple Locations.
keywords: representing the office in dealings with vendors
strategy: Apply in the opening window: it is only five days (October 26–30, 2026), and Direct Hire announcements can close early or fill fast, so have your resume ready beforehand.

Rewrite each IEM entry around the specialized experience list, giving 3 or more concrete examples for each grade you apply for (logistics, budget tracking, vendor coordination, data analysis, reports), all in your own words. The posting says copied text will not count.

Keep your resume to two pages. For each job, list the month/year dates, hours per week, and title, and frame IEM work in federal terms, such as 'supported state/local government clients' and 'coordinated deployment logistics.'
Apply at GS-11 only unless you can honestly show a full year of GS-11-level independent evaluation, advisory, and commitment-making work. Promotion potential to GS-12 exists anyway.
Answer the questionnaire honestly. Rate yourself 'expert' only where a resume bullet proves it, since the posting warns that overstatement can remove you from consideration.
Use your people skills under 'liaison' and 'representing the office' examples, but lead with administrative operations content rather than policy expertise.
resume_bullets: Coordinated [logistics/travel/procurement] for [number] staff supporting [client agency] disaster [recovery/preparedness] operations, managing [budget amount] and tracking expenditures in [system]. ([hours] hrs/wk)
Analyzed [type of data, e.g., staffing or cost data] from [sources] to identify trends and prepared [reports/briefings] for [audience], leading to [verified outcome].
Served as primary liaison with [vendors/government counterparts], negotiating [agreements/schedules] and resolving [type of issue] to keep [project] on time.
interview_questions: Tell us about a time you identified an inefficient administrative process and improved it.
Describe your experience managing a budget, procurement, or vendor relationship. What went wrong, and how did you handle it?
How would you prioritize competing requests from management in fleet, space, and HR at the same time?
Give an example of handling a stressful, fast-changing situation while maintaining attention to detail.
watch_outs: The application window is very short (October 26–30, 2026) and the job is not telework- or remote-eligible; check which duty locations are actually near Manassas.
A Secret clearance and background investigation are required, which can delay your start date.
Fleet management and budget duties are central. If your IEM work was mostly planning or policy, you may struggle to show 3 or more specialized experience areas.
This is ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations; make sure you are comfortable with the mission and the politically visible environment.
